newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-GIANT-KILLER WADDLE DELIGHTED AFTER WONDER GOAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GIANT-KILLER WADDLE DELIGHTED AFTER WONDER GOAL.

text.p: The great enduring attraction of the F.A. Cup is that it never stops providing unlikely winners and heroes.

On Saturday former England international winger Chris Waddle, who has twice experienced the despair of playing in losing Cup finals with Tottenham in 1987 and Sheffield Wednesday in 1993, enjoyed some totally unexpected Cup glory as lowly Bradford City stunned premier league Everton with a 3-2 fourth round win at Goodison Park.
Now 36, slower than in his heyday at Newcastle, Spurs, Marseille and Wednesday when he earned 62 England caps, but still with marvellous skill on the ball, Waddle was one of the day's heroes.

He scored an outstanding goal in Bradford's win and had a hand in all of Bradford's important moves which helped them reach the fifth round -- or its equivalent -- for the first time since 1988 and for only the seventh time since they won the Cup for the only time in their history in 1911.
And as Waddle, a former sausage-factory worker who started his career at tiny Tow Law Town in the north east, said afterwards: "I have never been a giant-killer before -- it's a nice feeling."

Not only that but he said the goal he scored to put Bradford 2-0 up was one of the best he had ever scored in a 17-year professional career, which has included a European Cup final appearance with Marseille.
Waddle found the back of the net from 35 metres, chipping over goalkeeper Neville Southall after Andrei Kanchelskis gave the ball away.
"I thought Andrei was going to pass the ball back to Neville," said Waddle. "Maybe he should have done but when it came to me I thought why not?' When it dropped in it was a great feeling.
"I've scored some great goals in my career but that is up there with the best of them.
"Myself and Rob Steiner will probably get the headlines but it was a great team performance all round."
Bradford travelled to Goodison rated as 250-1 outsiders to win the Cup and with not very much going for them. A poor run of results has seen them slip to 22nd in the first division.
But Everton are currently a demoralised outfit, having lost their last five league matches with their only win since the middle of December coming against first division Swindon in the third round.
And Bradford were the ones who best shrugged off their league form, going ahead through John Dreyer after 49 minutes and doubling that lead when Waddle scored two minutes later.

They shrugged off Andrew O'Brien's 54th-minute own goal with Steiner making it 3-1 in the 59th minute. Gary Speed gave Everton a glimmer of hope with Everton's second just before the end but Bradford held out for the final few seconds.

Manager Chris Kamara, who has Waddle under contract until the end of the season after picking him up free from Scottish first division Falkirk, told how Southall had asked in the tunnel before the match if Waddle was playing.
"Chris told him he was and I said to Nev you had better stay on your line then!"' said Kamara.
"The goal was fantastic. Once the ball went to him everyone in the dug-out said it was a goal.
"I've been telling everyone Chris shouldn't be with us, he should still be in the premier league.
"No-one would take a chance with him but I was quite happy to have him with me and I am sure he still believes he should be playing at the top."
Kamara said he felt the 3-2 scoreline flattered Everton and added: "I said before the game Chris Waddle would be the best player on the pitch and I was right."
Everton boss Joe Royle admitted: "We are desperately disappointed and embarrassed. Since winning the Cup the first division clubs have been a curse to us -- or we have been a curse to ourselves.
"One of the goals was a brilliant finish but our defending for a premier league side, not just today but for several matches, has been very poor.
"We created enough chances to win several games but we are out and it is very hard to take in.
"Waddle's was a great finish but there is no doubt we contributed to all three and then we ended up playing desperation football."
